GATE 4 is pre-authorised for the eleven remaining surfaces on a stated condition (gate4PreAuthorised), so a session applies an approved surface without stopping - but a finalizer FAIL or a fresh NEEDS DECISION still pauses that one surface. RED Two defects were found in copy this system had already approved: splash.html promises that the updater checks for a newer build and NOTHING in the app ever called the updater, and tauri.conf.json carried a plugins.updater.dialog key the plugin does not accept. Both were found by grepping for the mechanism rather than for the words, which is the sharpened form of the 2026-09-05 clause about approved artefacts holding claims nobody re-reads. RED And the story lint hook is blind to copy inside a code fence, so on the slot-shaped surfaces - cli-strings, and any .tsx copy - the fact-checker and a human reader are the only real gate; a green hook there is not evidence. | 2026-09-07 later: the analytics opt-out was removed by the owner mid-run, which re-opened a recorded surface - the first time that has happened here. The handling worth repeating: the words were changed in the CLICK DUMMY first and the reason written into the design README beside them (section 10a), so the person who reads the dummy to approve it sees why it changed; only then did the app follow. The voice decision inside that change was to KEEP the "Never sent" list against an instruction to keep it to one line, because band R delivers reassurance as a specific refusal and a notice with nothing checkable in it is an announcement. 🔴 And the cli-strings writer PROVED the fenced-copy blindness on its own file rather than citing the precedent: two banned words inside a slot fence went undetected (exit 0), the same two words in the commentary were both named (exit 2). That is a reproducible two-command proof and it belongs in the global record.
